title: Comcast's "fiber-powered Wi-Fi" is just cable, AT&T says in false advertising case
author: Jon Brodkin
summary_long: AT&T on Friday accused Comcast of false advertising in a lawsuit challenging the marketing claim that Comcast's cable broadband service and Wi-Fi is "fiber-powered." "This case challenges Comcast’s false advertising campaign for its residential Internet service, marketed under the Xfinity brand to consumers nationwide," AT&T's lawsuit said. "At the center of that campaign is Comcast’s claim that Xfinity Internet and its associated Wi-Fi service are 'Fiber-Powered.'" While Comcast has deployed plenty of fiber throughout the US, its cable Internet service makes the final connection to homes with coaxial cable. This results in upload speeds being far slower than download speeds. Read full article Comments Source: arstechnica.com. Date: 2026-11-16. id: bigtech:robosoldier startup backed by eric trump misses payroll may :2026-11-16T22:58:27.000Z
title: Robo-soldier startup backed by Eric Trump misses payroll, may collapse
author: Jeremy Hsu
summary_long: A humanoid robotics company backed and advised by President Donald Trump’s son, Eric Trump, has reportedly missed payroll and may be on the brink of collapse after a funding shortfall. The Silicon Valley startup, Foundation Future Industries, claims it is developing and testing robots for military roles on battlefields from Ukraine to Gaza. Foundation failed to pay employees for the payroll period ending on October 30, anonymous sources told CNBC. The startup’s staff is especially angry because Foundation’s co-founder and CEO, Sankaet Pathak, supposedly borrowed $4.6 million in company funds to buy a luxury home overlooking San Francisco Bay about a year ago. id: bigtech:three small failures combined to take down microsoft 365:2026-11-16T21:56:39.000Z
title: Three small failures combined to take down Microsoft 365
author: Nick Indge
summary_long: A hidden defect in Microsoft's cloud gateway, dormant since July, was to blame for one of the largest outages in the company's history last week. A preliminary Post-Incident Report (PIR) released by the company outlines how the latent bug, changes in traffic, and reduced server capacity combined to knock much of Microsoft 365 and Exchange infrastructure offline at the end of last week. Microsoft's report lists the incident's final status as "a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents." Microsoft's preliminary report places the outage between November 12 at 16:20 UTC and November 13 at 16:10 UTC, just under 24 hours total, and additional monitoring remained in place for any affected systems through November 14. The outage started on November 12 and quickly rippled through businesses and public offices that depend on Microsoft's cloud and email exchange infrastructure. Source: arstechnica.com.
